title: Liverpool vs. Man City Combined XI: Only Four Reds Selected
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray4:00 PM EDTSunday’s match will be brimming with superstars. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Van Dijk), Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty Images (Haaland)The Premier League weekend’s headline act delivers a superstar-laden contest between two of England’s behemoths: Liverpool and Manchester City.

Following a three-week international break, Sunday’s tantalizing clash at Anfield is the perfect tonic—even if the majority of the discourse surrounding the fixture centers around Man City being found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial regulations on a mass scale.
Many of the division’s leading talents will take to the field on Merseyside, with both clubs boasting expensively-assembled rosters brimming with elite players.
With that in mind, here’s how a combined XI of available Liverpool and City players looks.

Alisson has set the standard over the past decade. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesLiverpool and City both have the luxury of exceptional first-choice goalkeepers and the battle between Alisson and Gianluigi Donnarumma is certainly not clear-cut. Two phenomenal shot-stoppers with the odd error coded into their game, they stand among the world’s best in their position.

But, when injury-free, Alisson just edges this particular duel with his more consistent showings in Liverpool’s goal. The Brazilian is superior with the ball at his feet and an unmatched master of one-vs.-one situations.

Matheus Nunes is super consistent. / Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesRonald Araújo has made an excellent start to his loan spell at Anfield as a repurposed right back, but the consistency and quality of Matheus Nunes still prevails. The Portuguese defender remains a hugely underappreciated talent.

Nunes has an incredibly complete game. Boasting endless energy reserves, terrific physicality and impressive defensive intelligence for a former box-to-box midfielder, he’s one of the most reliable fullbacks in the Premier League.

Rúben Dias is a calming presence. / Matt McNulty/Getty ImagesThere are some fantastic center backs prowling Liverpool and City’s defensive lines, but few possess the blend of power, composure and leadership owned by Rúben Dias. While perhaps not quite as imperious as during his earliest years at the Etihad Stadium, he’s still a formidable presence.

The 29-year-old is not blessed with super recovery speed or a goalscoring knack, but his defensive positioning and incredible understanding of his role makes him ever so reliable. Dias seldom puts a foot wrong for the Cityzens.

Virgil van Dijk is still going strong aged 35. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesMarc Guéhi and the emerging Jérémy Jacquet are both impressive talents, but Virgil van Dijk is the greatest defender of the past decade—even if, like Dias, he’s not quite as commanding or flawless as he was several years ago.
Van Dijk’s reputation was somewhat knocked by being forced to babysit Ibrahima Konaté for large stretches of last season, but Jacquet’s arrival has allowed Liverpool’s skipper to shine once again.
Plus, he’s always good for a vital goal from a set piece.

Man City’s left back options are far superior. /  James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesCity arguably have three left backs better than Liverpool’s Milos Kerkez. Nico O’Reilly and Rayan Aït-Nouri are quality options for Enzo Maresca, but it’s the effortlessly imposing Joško Gvardiol who has been trusted in the role by the Italian early in his reign.

The Croatian defender has the stature and physicality of a center half—a role he’s played regularly throughout his career—yet the grace and technical class to consistently grab goals and assists when rampaging up the flank.

Elliot Anderson’s ascent has been so impressive. / Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesWhen Elliot Anderson was sold to Nottingham Forest to help Newcastle United comply with the Premier League’s financial regulations, few predicted he would be valued at $153 million just two years later. Yet, here we are.

The Englishman’s ascent has been rather remarkable, with his place as a guaranteed starter for City and England well earned. The combative midfielder is capable of operating as a No. 6 and No. 8 courtesy of his relentless engine and unrivaled industry.

Dominik Szoboszlai was outstanding last season. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesThe Argentine duo of Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernández are both top-level midfielders, while the same can be said of Ryan Gravenberch. But Dominik Szoboszlai’s powerful, all-action performances make him the perfect partner for Anderson in a combined team.

The Hungarian generally thrives when operating closer to the opposition goal, but his displays at right back have underscored his defensive resilience. Few Liverpool players since Steven Gerrard have struck a ball more cleanly—or been more reliable providers of wonder goals.
